<reason>Both sides argued at a high level, but PRO (B) built the cleaner decisive path. CON's strongest move was the "consent is the delivery mechanism" frame plus the sharp distinction between recolonisation (Germany/France) and vast federal parks (Yellowstone) on one hand and deliberate release into inhabited farmland on the other — a genuine burden-setting hit that made PRO's opening evidence look off-target. But PRO met that burden squarely and specifically in Rebuttal 2 with Central Idaho 1995 (release into national forest ringed by ranches over a legislature that formally refused cooperation), Mexican wolves on working rangeland, Jura/Slovenia lynx over hunter and farmer protest, and Scottish sea eagles over crofter fury. That is exactly the category CON said did not exist, and it was plausible closed-book knowledge rather than fake precision. PRO also converted CON's own concession — "consent is purchasable" — into the debate's pivot with a well-aimed pressure question: what happens when the cheque is refused? CON's answer ("move, redesign, fund the cull properly in the meantime") was honest but self-damaging, because CON had already conceded in its opening that deer control is a chronic policy failure; PRO correctly crystallised this as "wait for consent and cull harder are the same policy, and it produced the bare hills CON conceded." CON's late reframe — that the motion's metric is ecological function, not mere predator survival, so a suppressed, hunted, contested population restores nothing — was the best thing in its case and kept a live route open. It just arrived at the close and rested on an unsupported assertion, and PRO had already blunted it: Idaho still holds hundreds under hunting seasons, France shoots a quota while numbers rise, and no government has asked its predators to leave. Grounding and format compliance were comparable (both sides clipped twice; both used proper A1/A2 labels). PRO simply made the choice easier to decide.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>PRO's answer to CON's Q1 in Rebuttal 2: CON demanded a deliberate release into inhabited farming country over declared objection that thrived, excluding recolonisation and big federal parks; PRO delivered Central Idaho, Mexican wolves on rangeland, Jura/Slovenia lynx and Scottish sea eagles, then flipped the framing ("rule out every category of success and you can declare anything untested"). Paired with PRO's "what happens when the cheque is refused?" question, which forced CON back onto a status quo it had already conceded has failed.</best_rebuttal>
